chunks: From him, from one of his companions, from Hanaan ibn Sadeer who said:

I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) at the food-spread, so I inclined towards the endive. He said to me: 'O Hanaan, why are you not eating the leek?' I said, 'Because of what has come from you regarding the reports about the endive.' He said: 'And what is that which has come from us?' I said, 'It is said from you that you said that a drop falls upon it from Paradise every day.' He said: 'So upon the leek, then, seven drops.' I said, 'So how should I eat it?' He said: 'Cut off its roots and throw away its heads.'

key_terms.الْكُرَّاثَ: Leek, a type of allium vegetable
key_terms.الْهِنْدَاءِ: Endive, a type of leafy vegetable

ai.seo_question: Why did Hanaan avoid eating leeks and how did the Imam instruct him to consume them?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia scholarly principle of distinguishing between authentic, actionable traditions and popular or weak reports (khabar al-wahid) that may cause unnecessary asceticism. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects Hanaan’s hesitation by clarifying that the 'seven drops' were likely a metaphorical or exaggerated interpretation, instructing him to consume the leek after removing the roots and heads to mitigate any perceived negative effects. This demonstrates the practical application of hadith in daily life, where dietary habits are guided by scholarly interpretation rather than rigid adherence to every reported detail.
